Reverse-engineer the JAVASCRIPT syntax highlighter's exact token stream. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping snippets in a
fenced block whose info string is `javascript`.
Also check whether alias `js` behaves identically, and probe `typescript`/`ts` and `jsx` separately (record if they differ).

Adjacent tokens sharing a CSS class are MERGED into one span; unclassed tokens are bare escaped text.

Cover exhaustively:
- Keywords (`k`/`kd`/`kr`/`kc`): var let const function return if else for while do switch case break continue new delete typeof instanceof in of this class extends super import export from default async await yield try catch finally throw void with debugger; true false null undefined NaN Infinity; which get `kd`, which `kr`, which `kc`.
- Builtins (`nb`): Array Boolean Date Error Function JSON Math Number Object RegExp String console document window Promise Symbol Map Set - and which are `nb` vs `nx`.
- Identifiers `nx`; property access; function names in a function declaration (`nf`? `nx`?); class names; object literal keys; labels.
- Numbers: `mi`, `mf`, `mh`, `mo`, `mb`, exponents, BigInt, numeric separators.
- Strings: `s1` single, `s2` double, template literals (backtick) including interpolation, escapes (`se`), regex literals (`sr`) and how the lexer decides regex-vs-division (probe an assignment of a regex literal versus a chain of divisions).
- Comments: `c1` line, `cm` block, jsdoc.
- Operators `o` and punctuation `p`: assignment, equality, strict equality, relational, arithmetic, exponent, increment, logical, nullish, optional chaining, arrow, spread, bitwise, shifts, compound assignment, ternary, comma, semicolon, colon, dot, parens, brackets, braces. Determine which chars are `o` vs `p`.
- Whitespace: when is whitespace `w` vs unclassed? Probe indentation and spaces around operators.
- Errors `err` for invalid characters (hash, at-sign).
- Arrow functions, destructuring, spread, classes, generators, async/await, decorators.
- Non-ASCII/Chinese inside strings and comments.

## Probe harness (already built, do not rewrite it)

`/tmp/probe/p.mjs` is an ESM module exporting:
- `run({a,b,c,d,e,f})` -> full stdout string (any omitted key defaults to a marker like 'MKAA')
- `phase(slot, text)` -> the isolated output of one pipeline stage:
  - slot `'a'`,`'b'`,`'c'` => `markdown.markdown(text)` with NO extensions
  - slot `'d'` => `extensions=['extra','tables']`
  - slot `'e'` => `extensions=['codehilite','fenced_code']`
  - slot `'f'` => `extensions=['toc']`
  - slot `'5'` => phase5: `extensions=['extra','tables','codehilite','fenced_code','toc']`, `output_format='xhtml'`
- `phase5(text)`, `full(a,b,c,d,e,f)`

Write your own throwaway driver scripts under `/tmp/work/<yourname>/` that `import { phase, run, full } from '/tmp/probe/p.mjs'`
and print `JSON.stringify` of every result so whitespace is unambiguous. Batch MANY cases per node process
(each executable invocation costs ~0.5s; a batch of 60 cases in one node process is fine and takes ~30s).

## Rules
- The ONLY source of truth is running `/workspace/dataset/test19_executable`. Never run `python`/`python3` (not available).
- Never guess from memory of the Python libraries: every claim in your spec must be backed by an observed probe.
  Where you DO rely on library knowledge to pick what to probe, that is fine - but the recorded behavior must be observed.
- You are producing a SPEC, not code. No implementation.

## Output
Write your exhaustive findings to `/tmp/specs/pyg-javascript.md`. Requirements for that file:
- Organised with headings; every rule stated precisely enough to implement without further probing.
- Include a large "Observed cases" section: a list of `INPUT (JSON-escaped)` -> `OUTPUT (JSON-escaped)` pairs
  covering everything you probed, including the boring confirmations and every edge case. Aim for 60+ concrete cases.
- Explicitly flag anything you could NOT determine, and anything surprising/counter-intuitive.
- Be exhaustive: this file is the only thing the implementer will read. Length is not a concern; omissions are fatal.

Then return (as your final message) a <=350 word summary: the top surprising/critical rules only.
